definitions.definition: (used after the hour) In the 12-hour period from midnight to noon (the first half of the day) when using the 12-hour clock.

quote.citation: 1967, United States Travel Service, Plant Tours for International Visitors to the United States, page 49:
quote.text: Greenfield [...] Monday thru Friday, 9 to 12 a.m.

quote.citation: 2001, Customs Service effects of proposed legislation on officers' pay, United States General Accounting Office, page 45:
quote.text: One of the most common night shifts is the 12 a.m.-to-8 a.m. shift.
We never say 12 a.m. or 12 p.m. It's either 12 midnight or 12 noon, respectively.

quote.citation: 2009, Robert Bill, Medical Mathematics and Dosage Calculations for Veterinary Professionals, page 348:
quote.text: The 12-hour clock uses A.M. for the morning hours of midnight (12:00 A.M.) to almost noon (11:59 A.M.) and the P.M. designation for the hours from noon (12:00 P.M.) to almost midnight (11:59 PM).

quote.citation: 2015, Arhlene A. Flowers, Global Writing for Public Relations, page 141:
quote.text: The 12-hour clock, which is used in the U.S., Canada, and a few other countries, divides time into two cycles: a.m. (ante meridiem, Latin for before midday) from midnight, 12 a.m., to 11:59 a.m.; and p.m. (post meridiem, Latin for after midday) from noon, 12 p.m., to 11:59 p.m.

quote.citation: 2021, Jukka Heinonen, Ortzi Akizu-Gardoki, Sanna Ala-Mantila, Energy Efficient Cities of Today and Tomorrow, page 196:
quote.text: The following daylight peaks are identified around lunchtime, from 12 am to 1 pm, while for weekend days, the curve show several daylight peaks from 7 am to late lunchtime, around 1 pm.
